chunks: Umayyah ibn ʿAmr narrated from al-Shaʿīrī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to say: "When the caller announces, it is not for you to increase. Then when he falls silent, it is for you to increase. The increase is only forbidden while the call is being heard, and silence makes it permissible."

key_terms.الزِّيَادَةُ: the act of raising the bid
key_terms.السُّكُوتُ: the silence that marks the point of permissibility
key_terms.الْمُنَادِي: the caller or announcer conducting the public sale
key_terms.تَزِيدَ: to increase the offer or bid

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to increase a bid during a public sale announcement?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning bidding during a public sale announcement. It states that increasing the bid is not permitted while the caller is actively announcing, but it becomes permissible once the announcement has ceased.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3979 - Umayyah ibn Amr narrated from Al-Sha'eeri, who narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), that Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said:

"When the caller (auctioneer) announces the price, it is not permissible for you to increase the bid. However, when the caller becomes silent, then you are allowed to increase the bid. Indeed, raising the bid is prohibited while the announcement is still being heard, but it becomes permissible when silence follows."
